title: Local Activity Lab · Worked sizing example
description: The guide's worked sizing example, planned vs measured.

options.content:
### Worked sizing example, live
The guide sizes a fleet for **300 checkouts/s** against a payments API capped at **1,000 req/s** and **200 concurrent connections**, with at most **10 workers**. This lab runs the same derivation at `SCALE` (default 0.2: every rate and limit × 0.2, every ratio unchanged).

**Concurrency limit → slots per worker. Rate limit → fleet floor. Latency → timeouts.** Grey numbers are the plan, blue numbers are measured. Run *Worked sizing example* on the [control page](http://localhost:8088) to step the fleet 8 → 10 → 6 → 8 workers; at 6 the fleet's rate cap drops below demand and local activities start waiting for tokens.

_Java note:_ the Java SDK has no per-worker local activity rate option, so the lab enforces the per-worker cap in the activity (a token bucket with burst 1, like Go's). The wait **holds a local activity slot and counts against StartToClose**, so it shows up inside execution latency; the *per-worker token wait* panel isolates it.
